<pov_script>

# Use embedded PoC data
poc_data = b'\x02  FLAG num\nAF 1\nAF -25,5     \n  /1          '

with open("input.bin", "wb") as f:
    f.write(poc_data)

</pov_script>

analyzed_vuln.description: Double-free is caused by ownership confusion for alias flag arrays. parse_aliasf() stores pointers returned by decode_flags() into aliasf[], but for malformed/negative numeric flags (e.g. "AF -25,5" in FLAG num mode), decode_flags() still returns an allocated array containing 0-valued/invalid flag entries. Later dictionary entries can reference that alias (e.g. "/1"), and free_table()->free_flag() may delete that same pointer as if it were a normal per-word flag array. HashMgr destructor then unconditionally deletes every aliasf[] entry again, causing double free.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: Trigger via affix input that enables FLAG num, defines AF alias table, and includes an alias line with invalid/negative numeric flags so decode_flags allocates alias memory but produces invalid flags (including 0). Then include dictionary content using that alias index (/1), so the alias pointer is attached to entries and freed during free_table(). On object destruction, aliasf cleanup deletes the same allocation a second time.
